newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 1.35 pct in selective rebound.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 1.35 pct in selective rebound.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose an average 1.35 percent amid selective buys led by shares of largely state-owned firms and utilities on Friday, rebounding from the index's 81,000 support, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed up 1,100.48 points at 82,541.80 after diving 3.84 percent in the last three days, following Monday's 1.03 percent rise to an all-time high close of 84,692.20.
Over the week, it lost 1.5 percent after last week's 1.5 percent gain.
Trade volume firmed to 14.95 trillion lira ($151.5 million) from 13.29 trillion ($134.9 million) on Thursday.

"Today's rise was in reaction to the recent drops, but it was a highly selective movement. Medium-term indicators still show that prices are overbought," said Haydar Haydaroglu from state-owned Halkbank.
"The index must ease to 79,500-80,000 range to build momentum for a healthy rise although there is technical support at 81,000," he added.
Sales earlier in the week followed a third attempt on critical resistance at the index's 85,000 level on Monday.
